hypotheses.title: Conditional Volume-Spike Bollinger Band Mean-Reversion (trade_when)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Historically, standardized Bollinger Band price displacement (-group_zscore((close - ts_mean(close, 10)) / ts_std_dev(close, 10), subindustry)) achieved a remarkable Sharpe of 2.43 on BRAIN, but generated high turnover (62%). By wrapping the signal in the state-conditional operator trade_when(volume > 1.5 * ts_mean(volume, 20), signal, -1), the alpha only executes during abnormal institutional volume surges (order flow exhaustion), holding existing positions (-1) during normal market noise. This cuts turnover dramatically to ~15-20%, mathematically boosting Fitness into the 1.50+ qualifying range with 100% universal instrument coverage.
confounders: Major structural earnings surprises where volume surges confirm a fundamental multi-month rerating
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails during prolonged runaway trends where volume spikes continue in the direction of the momentum.

hypotheses.title: Institutional Flow Confirmation via Return-Volume Cross-Correlation (ts_corr)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: In financial market microstructure, institutional accumulation generates positive co-movement between price returns and trading activity (ts_corr(returns, volume / adv20, 20) > 0). Conversely, negative price-volume correlation indicates distribution, where prices are marked up on dry volume and dumped on heavy liquidation volume. Standardizing this 20-day time-series correlation cross-sectionally by subindustry isolates pure institutional order flow direction with zero lookahead, 100% universal coverage, and zero correlation with accounting alphas.
confounders: Erratic volume spikes around index rebalancing dates
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if volume-return correlation reflects temporary retail frenzy rather than informed institutional positioning.

hypotheses.title: Realized Volatility Compression Squeeze Anomaly (ts_std_dev ratio)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Asset pricing theory and volatility clustering establish that asset volatility is mean-reverting. Extended periods of extreme volatility contraction (measured by the ratio of 20-day rolling return volatility to 252-day annual baseline volatility: ts_std_dev(returns, 20) / (ts_std_dev(returns, 252) + 0.0001)) represent volatility squeezes. Under subindustry neutralization, equities undergoing the most extreme volatility compression experience energetic directional breakout resolution, compensating liquidity providers.
confounders: Zombie firms with zero trading interest and perpetually flat volatility
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if compressed volatility persists for multiple quarters without mean-reverting.
